title: Le Blanc's denial of remitted-sins persuasion as formal act has wide Reformed backing
source_text: CXXVI. Quae cum ita sint, judicet aequus lector, & ipsa Viri Docti, qui Theses meas carpit, conscientia, num ab ipso jure reprehendar, tanquam is qui deseruerim doctrinam in Schola Reformata universim hactenus receptam; ac dolose & dissimulanter, & contra propriam meam conscientiam, obtrudere coner, seu doctrinam in eadem Schola probatam, opinionem quandam novitiam, & ante paucos tantum annos propositam & admissam a duobus vel tribus solum obscuri nominis inter Reformatos Ministris: Idque propterea quod negem actum formalem fidei salvificae, & cujus respectu ipsi tribuitur justificatio, esse persuasionem qua fideles singuli statuunt sibi esse remissa peccata? Quandoquidem palam est ea in re me sequi, aut astipulantes habere Viros in Schola Reformata, tum hoc seculo, tum superiori, Doctissimos & Celeberrimos, Zanchium, Martyrem, Musculum, Perkinsium, Davenantium Episcopum Sarisburiensem, qui Synodo Dordracenae & interfuit & subscripsit, Amesium Franekeranae Theologiae Professorem, Joannem Mestrezatium, apud Parisienses V. D. M. notissimum, Petrum Molinaeum filium, Theologiae Doctorem & Canonicum Cantuariensem, Antonium Walaeum Professorem Leydensem, Widmarium Professorem in Academia Groningana, & Christophorum Wittichium ante hac Noviomagi, & nunc Lugduni Batavorum Theologiae itidem Professorem, ac denique ipsam Confessionem Anglicanam, ante annos paulo minus quam triginta, Theologorum Presbyterianorum communi consensu conscriptam & editam. Ut omittam Theologos ipsos quorum testimonia mihi objicit vir Doctus, Rivetum, Wendelinum, & Davidem Paraeum; quibus addere possunt Robertum Baronium Professorem Aberdonensem, & Samuelem Maresium Professorem Groninganum, idem mecum hac in parte sentire, & docere verbis disertis & expressis; licet alioqui mihi non omnino probetur eorum in hac quaestione doctrina.
pass_a_gloss: These things being so, let the fair reader judge, and the conscience of the Learned Man who carps at my theses, whether I am justly rebuked by him as one who has deserted the doctrine universally received until now in the Reformed School; and who deceitfully and dissemblingly, against my own conscience, try to thrust forward — or as doctrine approved in that same School — a certain novel opinion proposed and admitted only a few years ago by two or three ministers of obscure name among the Reformed: and that because I deny that the formal act of saving faith, and that with respect to which justification is attributed to it, is the persuasion by which individual believers judge their sins remitted to them? Since it is plain that in this matter I follow, or have as assenting, men in the Reformed School both of this and the former century, most learned and celebrated: Zanchi, Martyr, Musculus, Perkins, Davenant Bishop of Salisbury who both attended and subscribed the Synod of Dort, Ames professor of theology at Franeker, John Mestrezat most noted V.D.M. among the Parisians, Peter Du Moulin the son, Doctor of Theology and Canon of Canterbury, Antony Walaeus Leiden professor, Widmar professor in the Groningen Academy, and Christopher Wittich formerly at Nijmegen and now likewise theology professor at Leiden, and finally the Anglican Confession itself, composed and published a little less than thirty years ago by common consent of Presbyterian theologians. Not to mention the very theologians whose testimonies the Learned Man objects to me — Rivet, Wendelin, and David Pareus — to whom can be added Robert Baron Aberdeen professor and Samuel Maresius Groningen professor, as sensing the same with me on this point and teaching it in clear express words; though otherwise their doctrine on this question is not altogether approved by me.
pass_b_english: Fair readers — and the opponent's conscience — should judge whether denying remitted-sins persuasion as faith's formal justifying act deserts universal Reformed doctrine, or foists a novel fringe view.
Le Blanc's side includes Zanchi, Martyr, Musculus, Perkins, Davenant (Dort subscriber), Ames, Mestrezat, young Du Moulin, Walaeus, Widmar, Wittich, and the Anglican Confession (~30 years earlier).
Even Rivet, Wendelin, Pareus — plus Baron and Maresius — teach the same point in express words, though Le Blanc does not fully approve their wider account on this question.

choices.why: Opponent's charge; Le Blanc lists counter-authorities.
